messages:
maya: quick follow-up on the stride controller idea from the autoscale RFC — thinking about clear admission boundaries between the controller and allocator. wanted to capture tradeoffs before i write the follow-up doc.

drew: +1. i sketched two models last week: tight-coupled admission (controller makes final admit/reject) vs. deferred-admission (controller emits intent, allocator enforces).

maya: summary of concern: if controller does final admit we get simpler failover but blow up coupling/latency on scale. if allocator does it we have looser semantics but better isolation.

jia: agree. also consider the failure modes: controller losing leader should not deadlock admission. if allocator owns final admit, it can continue on stale intents with backpressure.

leo: reactive thought — what about split responsibility by SLO class? controller final-accept for high-priority tenants (SLA-backed), allocator final-accept for best-effort. keeps fast path for critical traffic.

maya: that's interesting. it maps to our pricing/tiers too. but raises complexity in operator surface and audits (who took decision?).

sam: small nit: we need consistent accounting for burst credits. if both decide, we double-count or miss-charge. need single source of truth for credit ledger.

maya: agreed. ledger should be authoritative in allocator. controller should just annotate intent with desired credit delta. allocator mutates ledger when it accepts.

orca-bot: deploy-check: staging autoscaler rollout at 22:30 UTC — no blockers shown.

leo: another tradeoff: latency vs correctness. sample flow: controller emits intent, allocator can accept immediately for warm pools, else call out to prewarm queue. that keeps controller nonblocking.

maya: sketch of a proto-policy (rough):
```
policy: 
  intent_ttl: 30s
  final_decider: allocator
  high_priority_override: controller
  ledger_authority: allocator
  fallback: model-variant-route
```

jia: looks good. intent_ttl is key. short ttl prevents leaked intents if controller restarts. also need idempotent intent ids.

drew: +1 on idempotency. also add a reconcile loop in allocator to garbage-collect orphaned intents older than 2x ttl.

sam: ops question: what observability do we need? I want per-intent lifecycle traces: created_by, matched_pool, accept_ts, reject_reason. we should emit a span for the handoff.

maya: yes. add an event stream: intent.created, intent.handshake, intent.accepted/rejected, ledger.mutated. link with existing console dashboards.

leo: edge case: simultaneous intents for same tenant burst -> allocator should serialise by tenant token to avoid racey ledger updates. can use optimistic CAS on ledger entry + retry.

jia: agree, and support a small per-tenant admission window (100 ms) to coalesce bursts into one acceptance attempt. reduces churn.

maya: ok action items: 1) i'll draft follow-up doc with these boundaries and example config 2) drew to prototype allocator reconcile GC + ledger CAS logic 3) sam to add event schema to telemetry backlog 4) leo/jia will diagram failure scenarios.

drew: timeline?

maya: aim for draft by EOW, prototype next sprint.

sam: sounds good. adding :thumbsup:

orch-bot: note: created issue INF-1421 "stride controller admission boundaries follow-up" for this thread.

maya: thanks all — i'll ping when draft is up.
